name: Daniel Brady, barber

proprietors.name: Daniel Brady
proprietors.basis: ADOPTED, NOT MINTED. Daniel Brady is the reconstructed trade head the resident band's `trade_households` stage drew at barber_surgeon in the south division (slot trade_households:persons/male/20_29/south/family/trade:barber_surgeon:004), and that card says itself that the business band adopts these heads rather than minting its own. One quota, filled once: this house is the establishment that head keeps.

locations.basis: A FACE, NOT A PREMISES. The placement rule for a barber surgeon kept by a south-division household deals this house onto Lake Street; the face is drawn on the seed printed in `reconstruction.seed` from the faces that rule allows, and no lot, roof or coordinate is claimed. T-1195 writes the placement policy with its evidence and T-1199 seats this house on the lot grid.
locations.limit_reason: No source places this house, because no source names it: it exists because its keeper does. The street is the reconstruction's own deal and stops there.

dates.basis: NOTHING DATES THIS HOUSE. Its keeper was dealt onto the scene date and carries no arrival the layer can read; the record claims that the house was trading on 1835-07-01 and nothing about either end.

proprietor_community.basis: The 1 keeper(s) this record names and the resident layer holds a card for all read irish: Daniel Brady (irish). A house is not its keeper, so the reading is an inference about the house and is capped there.

replaceable_by: A register, directory or deed naming a real barber surgeon in the south division in 1835 — that house takes this slot and this record is withdrawn with the head it belongs to.

person.note: A DRAWN KEEPER, NOT A SHORTFALL. The December 1835 State census enumerates no barber surgeon, so the order book holds no bucket of this class to point at and no count of it is short. What is committed is the PERSON: the trade stage dealt Daniel Brady at this trade out of the 1839 trade table, and the premises ruling gives the trade a barber's shop. The house is what was missing, and it is withdrawn with the head.

basis.note: the trade stage drew 1 head(s) at barber surgeon in the south division and the premises ruling gives that trade a shop of its own. The style is dealt on the seed printed beside it from the period forms the register itself carries: the plainest form the register carries — a keeper's name against a trade line, as 'Frederick Thomas, drugs and paints' prints — because the register prints no barber's house whose form could be copied. The goods line is the trade in the resident layer's own word. No barber's notice survives in this corpus, so no goods line of the class exists to take and none is composed.

reconstruction.withdrawn_if: the retirement of the head itself, a re-ruling that gives this trade no premises of its own, or a source naming a real house of this trade; the retirement runs through --build, never by hand
